From 0d3f6d297bfb7af24d0508460fdb3d1ec4903fa3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Martin KaFai Lau <kafai@fb.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2015 11:51:06 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] ipv6: Avoid creating RTF_CACHE from a rt that is not managed
 by fib6 tree

The original bug report:
https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1272571

The setup has a IPv4 GRE tunnel running in a IPSec.  The bug
happens when ndisc starts sending router solicitation at the gre
interface.  The simplified oops stack is like:

__lock_acquire+0x1b2/0x1c30
lock_acquire+0xb9/0x140
_raw_write_lock_bh+0x3f/0x50
__ip6_ins_rt+0x2e/0x60
ip6_ins_rt+0x49/0x50
~~~~~~~~
__ip6_rt_update_pmtu.part.54+0x145/0x250
ip6_rt_update_pmtu+0x2e/0x40
~~~~~~~~
ip_tunnel_xmit+0x1f1/0xf40
__gre_xmit+0x7a/0x90
ipgre_xmit+0x15a/0x220
dev_hard_start_xmit+0x2bd/0x480
__dev_queue_xmit+0x696/0x730
dev_queue_xmit+0x10/0x20
neigh_direct_output+0x11/0x20
ip6_finish_output2+0x21f/0x770
ip6_finish_output+0xa7/0x1d0
ip6_output+0x56/0x190
~~~~~~~~
ndisc_send_skb+0x1d9/0x400
ndisc_send_rs+0x88/0xc0
~~~~~~~~

The rt passed to ip6_rt_update_pmtu() is created by
icmp6_dst_alloc() and it is not managed by the fib6 tree,
so its rt6i_table == NULL.  When __ip6_rt_update_pmtu() creates
a RTF_CACHE clone, the newly created clone also has rt6i_table == NULL
and it causes the ip6_ins_rt() oops.

During pmtu update, we only want to create a RTF_CACHE clone
from a rt which is currently managed (or owned) by the
fib6 tree.  It means either rt->rt6i_node != NULL or
rt is a RTF_PCPU clone.

It is worth to note that rt6i_table may not be NULL even it is
not (yet) managed by the fib6 tree (e.g. addrconf_dst_alloc()).
Hence, rt6i_node is a better check instead of rt6i_table.

Fixes: 45e4fd26683c ("ipv6: Only create RTF_CACHE routes after encountering pmtu")
Signed-off-by: Martin KaFai Lau <kafai@fb.com>
Reported-by: Chris Siebenmann <cks-rhbugzilla@cs.toronto.edu>
Cc: Chris Siebenmann <cks-rhbugzilla@cs.toronto.edu>
Cc: Hannes Frederic Sowa <hannes@stressinduktion.org>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/ipv6/route.c b/net/ipv6/route.c
index c8bc9b4ac328..74907c58a5c7 100644
--- a/net/ipv6/route.c
+++ b/net/ipv6/route.c
@@ -1322,6 +1322,12 @@ static void rt6_do_update_pmtu(struct rt6_info *rt, u32 mtu)
 	rt6_update_expires(rt, net->ipv6.sysctl.ip6_rt_mtu_expires);
 }
 
+static bool rt6_cache_allowed_for_pmtu(const struct rt6_info *rt)
+{
+	return !(rt->rt6i_flags & RTF_CACHE) &&
+		(rt->rt6i_flags & RTF_PCPU || rt->rt6i_node);
+}
+
 static void __ip6_rt_update_pmtu(struct dst_entry *dst, const struct sock *sk,
 				 const struct ipv6hdr *iph, u32 mtu)
 {
@@ -1335,7 +1341,7 @@ static void __ip6_rt_update_pmtu(struct dst_entry *dst, const struct sock *sk,
 	if (mtu >= dst_mtu(dst))
 		return;
 
-	if (rt6->rt6i_flags & RTF_CACHE) {
+	if (!rt6_cache_allowed_for_pmtu(rt6)) {
 		rt6_do_update_pmtu(rt6, mtu);
 	} else {
 		const struct in6_addr *daddr, *saddr;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/ipv6/route.c`**
1. **New Function Added**: 
   - A new static function `rt6_cache_allowed_for_pmtu` is introduced. This function checks if a route (`rt`) is allowed to create a RTF_CACHE clone during Path MTU (PMTU) updates. It ensures that the route does not already have the RTF_CACHE flag set and is either a RTF_PCPU clone or has a valid `rt6i_node`.

2. **Modification in `__ip6_rt_update_pmtu` Function**:
   - The condition that checks if a route is a cache is modified. Instead of directly checking if `rt6->rt6i_flags & RTF_CACHE`, it now calls the new function `rt6_cache_allowed_for_pmtu(rt6)`. This change ensures that a RTF_CACHE clone is only created from routes that are managed by the fib6 tree.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The introduction of the `rt6_cache_allowed_for_pmtu` function encapsulates the logic for determining whether a route can create a RTF_CACHE clone during PMTU updates. This change is directly related to the bug fix, as it addresses the issue of creating a cache from a route that is not managed by the fib6 tree, which was causing the system to crash (oops). By centralizing this logic in a dedicated function, the code becomes cleaner and more maintainable, while also preventing the specific bug reported in the bug report.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
rt6->rt6i_flags & RTF_CACHE
nrt6 = ip6_rt_cache_alloc(rt6, daddr, saddr);
ip6_ins_rt(nrt6);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs when the `__ip6_rt_update_pmtu` function checks if the route has the `RTF_CACHE` flag set, which indicates that it is a cache route. If this condition is true, it attempts to allocate a new route using `ip6_rt_cache_alloc()`, which can create a route that is not managed by the fib6 tree (i.e., `rt6i_table` is NULL). When `ip6_ins_rt(nrt6)` is called, it leads to a null pointer dereference because the newly created route does not have a valid `rt6i_node`, causing an oops.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (!rt6_cache_allowed_for_pmtu(rt6)) {
nrt6 = ip6_rt_cache_alloc(rt6, daddr, saddr);
```
Reason:
The fix introduces a new function `rt6_cache_allowed_for_pmtu()` that checks whether the route is allowed to create a `RTF_CACHE` clone. It ensures that the route is either a `RTF_PCPU` clone or has a valid `rt6i_node`. By using this check before attempting to create a new route, the code prevents the creation of a cache route from an unmanaged route, thus avoiding the null pointer dereference and ensuring that only valid routes are processed during the PMTU update.
